newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 1.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** Indian stocks seen mixed in light trade as criminal case involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao postponed for a week
Rao's plea for protection against possible arrest was
turned down last week. On Monday, the supreme court said it exempted the former PM from appearing in court on the same day due to security threats.
** Indian stockmarkets shut on Wednesday for a national holiday
** India's largest private firm Reliance Industries' board meets on October 18 to release first half results for the six months ended September 30, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) says
A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities houses last week
found the petrochemical giant's first half net profit heading for a steep 25.8 percent fall to 4.7 billion rupees from the year ago.

** Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) renames BSE 100 National index to BSE 100 Index. BSE said in statement late on Monday that this was done because of changes in trading technology, longer trading periods and almost instantaneous availability of information across the country
The National index included prices of certain scrips from
other exchanges or weighted average of some popular scrips in other exchanges in order to reflect market movements at the national level

** Cable maker Sterlite Industries records a net profit of 1.4 billion rupees in 1995/96 (July-June) after group company Sterlite Communicatons was merged with the firm. The scheme of merger of Sterlite Communications with the company, already approved by shareholders of both the companies came into effect on April 1, 1996

** Modiluft is planning to meet its cash problems through a $100 million external commercial borrowing for which it has already signed a MoU with the Columbia group of financiers from the United States, the Times of India reports

** Liquor major, United Breweries (UB) will invest $29.85 million in 1996/97 in its overseas operations. This includes $18 million in African and Eastern (Near East), a UK registered wholly owned subsididary of Unilever Plc in the Gulf to take over distribution of liquor business
